title: Dungeon Rally: Toy Car Escape
description: A toy car must navigate through a dungeon arena collecting energy orbs while avoiding traps. The player controls the car's movement, manages a limited fuel resource that obeys conservation (fuel spent equals distance traveled), and can undo/redo movement steps to optimize their escape route through the dungeon.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a dungeon car escape game. Load both GLB assets: place the dungeon_warkarma model as the arena environment scaled to fill the scene, and place the ToyCar model inside the dungeon as the player-controlled vehicle scaled appropriately (roughly 1/10th of the dungeon). Set up a third-person camera that follows the car from behind and above using OrbitControls locked to the car's position. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two point lights inside the dungeon with orange tones to create a torch-lit atmosphere. Generate 8 glowing energy orbs (small emissive spheres) at random positions within the dungeon floor bounds. The car starts with 100 fuel units. Implement WASD keyboard controls: each key press moves the car one grid step (1 unit) in the corresponding direction and costs 1 fuel. Display a HUD overlay showing: fuel remaining, orbs collected out of 8, and move count. Implement a move history stack. Pressing Z undoes the last move (restores car position and refunds 1 fuel, un-collects any orb at that position). Pressing Y redoes an undone move (re-spends fuel, re-collects orb if present). Conservation law: total fuel spent plus fuel remaining must always equal 100. When the car moves within 1.5 units of an orb, collect it with a brief scale-up animation and hide it. Pressing R resets the car to start position but keeps fuel spent (no free reset). Pressing Shift+R does a full reset restoring all state. Collecting all 8 orbs before fuel runs out shows a victory message. Running out of fuel shows a defeat message. Add a subtle particle dust effect when the car moves. The dungeon should cast shadows from the point lights onto the floor. Ensure all 10-14 interaction steps are trackable: movement in 4 directions, undo, redo, collect orbs, soft reset, full reset, and camera orbit.
